I called ahead to explain the situation, expecting at least a basic level of understanding or professionalism. Instead, the person who answered immediately started shouting over me. He called the delay “laughable,” refused to let me explain, and went on about how this should be a “lesson” for me, along with how I'll be charged a fee.

What was most frustrating wasn’t even the policy - it was the complete lack of basic courtesy. I was not given a chance to speak, explain, or even have a normal conversation. Being talked down to and cut off repeatedly is unacceptable, especially from a customer-facing business.

To be clear, I have nothing against the establishment itself, but this individual’s behavior was shockingly unprofessional and easily one of the most obnoxious phone interactions I’ve had. If this is how customers are treated for something as common as a travel delay, it seriously undermines any confidence in the business.

A short story regarding my haircut with Brittany Dubowski

Lost and without hope, I wandered around Chicago like a scruffy dog. My hair was a mess and my confidence was low. I heard a soft buzzing in the distance; was it a weed wacker or a chain saw? NO! It was much more inviting. I hastily made my way to the entrance of a small and unassuming business with little decor but a warmth that caused my heart to glow. A woman named Brittany greeted me and smiled in a comforting way, giving me the confidence to follow her into a sequestered chair. I shyly requested that she do what she does best. She offered recommendations, tips and style choices that I rapidly processed. With haste and determination, she started on my hair. Like an artist, sculpting a god out of marble, her precision was unmatched. She worked for about 30 minutes sculpting, shaping, and trimming to take away not only the rag that sat atop my head but also the stress of a long work week. She spoke about life in a way that brought joy. Her electric energy provided an infectious excitement. She turned the chair around and began to wash my hair; she scrubbed away the clippings and my insecurities, resulting in a soft and natural sheen that brought a strange resurgence of confidence. A fantastic performance that would get her into Juliard, Harvard, or Cambridge if they compared what she was able to do to art. I left after paying with a newly found energy that resulted in compliments from family, friends, and strangers alike. I will certainly go back.

P.S. The give you a discount on the parking thing across the street.
